Reporting to the Deputy Fire Chief, Communications, Technology and Organizational Performance, the Division Chief (Data Analytics and Decision Support) provides strategic leadership and oversight of data analytics, business intelligence, organizational performance, information management and decision-support services for Toronto Fire Services.

The position leads multidisciplinary teams in delivering reliable, timely and actionable information to support evidence-based decision-making, operational planning, continuous improvement, public information, accreditation and organizational accountability.

Working collaboratively with senior leadership, operational divisions and external stakeholders, the Division Chief establishes data and information management strategies, governance frameworks and reporting priorities, ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, corporate policies and professional standards.

Major Responsibilities:

Provides strategic leadership and direction for data analytics, business intelligence, performance measurement, information management and decision-support services, including the development of strategies, governance frameworks, standards and priorities.
Leads and develops multidisciplinary teams, fostering an inclusive, accountable and high-performing environment focused on service excellence and continuous improvement.
Oversees analytical studies, dashboards, reporting platforms, data models, statistical tools and geographic information systems, providing strategic advice and recommendations to support operational planning, resource allocation, risk management and policy development.
Establishes performance measures and monitoring frameworks, supporting organizational performance analysis, strategic planning, accreditation, service reviews and continuous improvement initiatives, including Community Risk Assessments, Standards of Cover and annual program appraisals.
Provides oversight of data quality, information governance, records management, privacy, access, disclosure, retention and information stewardship, ensuring compliance with legislative and corporate requirements.
Manages operating and capital budgets, procurement, contracts, consultants and complex projects, ensuring effective governance, risk management and delivery.
Builds and maintains partnerships with City divisions, emergency service agencies, government, academia, vendors and other stakeholders, while monitoring emerging technologies and practices in analytics, artificial intelligence, GIS and public safety information management.

Key Qualifications:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Information Systems, Business Administration, Public Administration, Geography, Geomatics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive experience providing strategic leadership in data analytics, business intelligence, performance measurement, information management or decision-support services within a large, complex organization.
Extensive experience leading and managing multidisciplinary teams, including establishing priorities, overseeing performance, supporting staff development and driving organizational improvement.
Considerable experience applying business intelligence, statistical analysis, data management and geographic information systems to develop analytical studies, dashboards, reporting solutions and recommendations for senior leadership and external partners.
Considerable experience developing and implementing performance measurement frameworks, analytical reporting and data governance practices to support service planning, operational performance, data quality and evidence-based decision-making.
Considerable experience developing and implementing records and information management strategies, governance frameworks and digital information management solutions, including records retention, information lifecycle management and compliance requirements.
Considerable experience managing operating and capital budgets, procurement, contracts, consultants and complex projects.
Expert knowledge of information governance, privacy, access to information, records management and applicable legislation, including MFIPPA, PHIPA and the Archives and Recordkeeping Act, 2006.
Expert knowledge of analytical and reporting technologies such as Power BI, SQL, SQL Server Reporting Services, data warehouses, statistical software, data integration tools and ESRI ArcGIS.
Knowledge of quality management, accreditation and continuous improvement processes, including familiarity with Commission on Fire Accreditation International standards.
Familiarity with municipal government, emergency services, public safety operations or similarly complex operational environments.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, research and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex issues and provide practical recommendations.
Excellent communication, consultation, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills, including the ability to present complex technical information to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated political acuity, sound judgment and discretion in managing sensitive or confidential matters, competing priorities and organizational change.
Ability to exercise independent judgment, initiative and accountability while fostering collaborative, inclusive and high-performing teams.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and related business applications.
Professional certification in data analytics, business intelligence, agile and/or project management, quality management or a related discipline would be considered an asset.

jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Operations
jobs.description:
At Autism Nova Scotia, we believe in the power of belonging, connection, and community. Every day, our teams work alongside Autistic individuals, families, and communities to create opportunities, remove barriers, and help build a province where everyone feels valued and included.

Behind this meaningful work are the people, systems, and resources that help make it all possible. And that's where you come in!

We're looking for a Director of Finance and Operations to join our leadership team!

Are you someone who loves bringing clarity to complex challenges? Do you enjoy building strong systems, finding practical solutions, and helping an organization make thoughtful, informed decisions? Are you equally comfortable looking at the big picture and rolling up your sleeves to get things done?
If so, we'd love to hear from you!

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced financial professional who wants to bring their expertise to an organization making a meaningful difference across Nova Scotia.
Working closely with our Chief Executive Officer and leadership team, you'll play an important role in strengthening our financial sustainability, supporting our operations, and helping us plan confidently for the future.

This is a hands-on leadership position where strategy and practical financial management go hand in hand. You'll help guide important organizational decisions while remaining actively involved in the financial work that keeps everything moving.
Most importantly, you'll be joining a collaborative team of people who care deeply about the work they do and the communities they serve.

About the Role Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director of Finance and Operations provides leadership across Autism Nova Scotia's financial and operational functions.

You'll be a trusted partner to the CEO, Board of Directors, and organizational leadership team, helping translate financial information into meaningful insights, practical solutions, and sound decisions.
Your work will touch many parts of the organization, from financial planning and reporting to improving operational systems and supporting the teams delivering our programs and services.

We know that great financial leadership is about more than numbers. It's about helping people understand the resources available, plan thoughtfully, and feel confident in the decisions they make.

What You'll Be Doing Financial Leadership and Management

You'll help keep our financial foundations strong while supporting thoughtful planning for the future.
Lead and actively manage financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls.
Prepare and maintain annual budgets, financial statements, forecasts, and management reports.
Stay connected to day-to-day accounting activities, including general ledger management, reconciliations, accounts payable and receivable, cash flow, and month-end and year-end processes.
Provide clear, practical financial analysis and recommendations to the CEO and Board of Directors.
Prepare and present financial updates, budgets, and forecasts to the Board and relevant committees.
Coordinate our annual audit and support financial reporting requirements related to government funding, grants, and contracts.
Collaborate with Human Resources and our payroll administrator to support accurate and effective payroll processes.

Organizational Operations

You'll help create the systems and processes that make it easier for our teams to do their best work.
Oversee key operational functions, including administrative systems, facilities, procurement, contracts, vendors, and organizational assets.
Identify opportunities to make our processes clearer, more consistent, and more effective.
Work alongside organizational Directors to support thoughtful resource planning and service delivery.
Help strengthen the infrastructure and operational practices that support our growing and evolving organization.

Risk Management and Organizational Compliance

You'll bring a thoughtful, proactive approach to helping our organization operate responsibly and sustainably.
Maintain strong financial and operational controls that support accountability and good decision-making.
Ensure our practices align with applicable legislation, accounting standards, funding agreements, and regulatory requirements.
Monitor financial reporting and contractual obligations.
Identify emerging risks and opportunities for improvement, bringing practical recommendations forward.
Support clear, accessible policies, procedures, and documentation that help our teams work confidently and consistently.

Leadership and Collaboration

You'll be part of a leadership team that values collaboration, shared problem-solving, and bringing different perspectives to the table.
Contribute to organizational planning, strategy, and leadership decisions.
Be a trusted financial and operational resource for the CEO and Directors.
Lead, mentor, and support employees within the Finance and Operations portfolio.
Build positive working relationships with auditors, financial institutions, funders, vendors, and community partners.
Help foster a workplace culture grounded in respect, accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.

What You'll Bring We're looking for someone who brings strong financial expertise, sound judgment, and a genuine interest in using their skills to support meaningful community work.

You might be someone who enjoys solving a complicated financial puzzle, helping a colleague better understand their budget, or finding a simpler way to make a process work.

You understand that good financial management is both strategic and practical, and you enjoy being involved in both.

Here's what we're hoping you'll bring to the team:

A post-secondary degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
A CPA designation.
Five to seven years of progressive experience in accounting, financial management, or a related leadership role.
Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial statements, accounting processes, reconciliations, and internal controls.
Experience coordinating audits and managing financial reporting, funding, or contractual requirements.
Strong analytical and organizational skills, with an ability to identify challenges and develop thoughtful, practical solutions.
The ability to make financial information understandable and useful for colleagues with different backgrounds and areas of expertise.
A collaborative leadership approach and a genuine interest in helping others succeed.

Experience in a nonprofit, charitable, or publicly funded environment would be a wonderful asset.
We also recognize that professional experience and expertise can develop through different career paths. If this opportunity interests you and you believe you could make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply.

Why Join Autism Nova Scotia? Because the work you do behind the scenes can make an incredible difference in the communities we serve.

At Autism Nova Scotia, you'll be part of a team of dedicated people working toward a shared vision of a more inclusive province.

We value thoughtful ideas, genuine collaboration, and the different perspectives and strengths that each person brings to our organization.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:
Make a meaningful impact.
Your work will directly support the programs, services, and advocacy that make a difference for Autistic individuals and families across Nova Scotia.
Help shape our future.
You'll play an important role in strengthening our financial sustainability and supporting long-term organizational planning.
Bring your ideas to life.
You'll have opportunities to improve systems, strengthen processes, and help us find better ways of working.
Enjoy variety in your work.
This position offers a rewarding combination of strategic leadership, hands-on financial management, and organizational collaboration.
Be part of something meaningful.
You'll work alongside colleagues who care about inclusion, community, and creating positive change.

Our Commitment to Inclusion At Autism Nova Scotia, inclusion is at the heart of what we do, and it's something we continue to learn about, strengthen, and put into practice every day.

We know that people bring different experiences, perspectives, strengths, and ways of thinking and working. We believe those differences make our teams and our organization stronger.

We're committed to creating an accessible, respectful, and welcoming workplace where people feel valued, supported, and able to contribute in ways that are meaningful to them.

We particularly welcome applications from Autistic individuals and people whose perspectives and experiences have been underrepresented in traditional workplaces.

We also recognize that recruitment processes don't always work equally well for everyone. If there are accommodations or adjustments that would help you participate comfortably and meaningfully at any stage, please let us know. We're happy to work with you.

We'd Love to Hear From You! If you're a financial professional who enjoys working with people, strengthening systems, and contributing to work that matters, we'd be delighted to learn more about you.

Come bring your expertise, your ideas, and your unique perspective to Autism Nova Scotia. Together, we can continue building a stronger, more inclusive community.

Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

Join our team!

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Director FP&A and Capital Investment is a key member of the company’s finance team and is responsible for supporting all financial planning and analysis activities across the International Division of Top Aces Inc. The director will be responsible for the division’s annual budget process, financial forecasting, financial strategic planning and business performance analysis activities. Additionally, the director will be responsible for supporting the effort to enhance the company’s continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving profitability and efficiency. The director will provide project financial support, return on investment (ROI) analysis along with KPI development, measurement and analysis. The successful candidate will have demonstrable leadership competencies, strong attention to detail, and will work well under pressure in a fast-paced environment. The candidate will demonstrate a successful track record of working collaboratively in a dynamic environment and a matrix organizational structure.

Own the division’s annual budgeting and financial planning process (quarterly forecasts and strategic plan 5-year forecast) and review all associated financial plans and budgets.
Develop, lead, and manage core FP&A activities.
Lead the development of P&L, balance sheet and cash flow forecasts and partner with internal stakeholders to optimize working capital (prepayments, inventory) and cash flow generation.
Lead the development of scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis and risks & opportunities.

Oversee capex financial management and capex forecasting improvement initiatives.
Lead inventory financial management and work with key stakeholders to optimize the level of inventory.
Oversee the preparation of the International Division monthly management accounts, FP&A reports and dashboards, including presentations to SLT and the company’s Board of Directors.
Support the division’s Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to evaluate and review new business and investment opportunities, including new business pricing, client Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), Return on Investment (ROI), payback period and return on capital (RONA) analyses.
Support the executive team decision-making by providing insightful data and analysis with the objective of improving Top Aces’ profitability and efficiency.
Build and develop the skill sets of finance professionals under her/his direction.

Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree required with concentration in finance and/or accounting or comparable business field preferred.
CPA and/or MBA preferred
10-15 years of experience in relevant accounting, or financial leadership roles.
Significant expertise with data analysis and reporting.
Ability to handle multiple assignments on a timely basis with a high degree of accuracy.
High level of motivation and aptitude for problem solving, with a strong attention to detail.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills as well as strategic thinking to effectively interface with external stakeholders and the division’s Senior Leadership Team.
Ability to translate financial data into strategic insights.
Able to work in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, possessing a high sense of urgency.
Ability to perform all work in support of our Corporate Values of Excellence, Service, Integrity … Together.

Working Conditions:

May be required to travel from time to time
May be required to work overtime or longer hours when Top Aces Requires

Supervisory, Training and Advisory Responsibilities:

May be required to provide regular guidance, advice and training, as requested by the supervisor, to other employees supporting the function.

Occupational Health and Safety:

Employees are responsible for:

Working in compliance with Occupational Health and Safety acts and regulations
Following safe work practices and procedures and using safeguards and personal protective equipment
Reporting hazards (such as unsafe situations and activities) to their supervisor immediately.

Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR:

Position requires Level II clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program

By joining Top Aces, you will find:

A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;
Opportunities for development and growth;
Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;
A flexible schedule;
Attractive benefit plan.

Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

About Homefield
Homefield Sports Group is a leading recreational sports business with the mission of creating exceptional lifelong opportunities to play sports. Every week, thousands of people participate in Homefield’s leagues to play sports, meet new people, and enjoy a dose of friendly competition. We serve approximately 25,000 participants across 16 sports in the GTHA.

The Role
We are looking for our first finance leader in a role that pairs practical execution with big picture financial thinking. You will be responsible for day-to-day accounting, month-end close, cash flow visibility, annual budgeting, and financial planning & analysis. This is not a large-team environment. This is a roll-up-your-sleeves position with real accountability for results. Over time, you will build the systems, processes, and team that enable rapid expansion of a multi-entity sports organization.

You will work directly with Homefield’s CEO as a strategic business partner. You will be both:
Hands-on (owning financials, close, and core financial processes), and
Strategic (driving planning, decision support, performance management, and M&A integration).

As Homefield scales, this role has a clear path to CFO.

Who This Role Is For
This role is well-suited for someone who has helped to build or run the finance function in a rapidly growing small or mid-sized business. The ideal candidate enjoys working closely with both business operations and ownership, and will have three or more years of progressive accounting / finance experience. A CPA designation is preferred but not required.

Key Responsibilities
Financial Foundation & Control
Own month-end close, financial statements, and reporting
Manage AP, AR, and revenue tracking across leagues and seasons
Lead and oversee payroll
Prepare tax filings and support year-end with external accountants
Improve processes and controls as the business grows

Planning, Insight & Decision Support
Build and maintain cash flow forecasts and budgets
Design, implement, and report on monthly financial and operational KPIs (The Homefield Scoreboard)

Growth & Scale
Build scalable multi-entity and multi-site reporting
Support M&A integration
